norms.heading: Parties may agree upon referees or court shall appoint.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: In all cases of reference, the parties, except when an infant may be a party, may agree upon a suitable person or persons, not exceeding three; and, upon filing such agreement, the reference shall be ordered accordingly. If the parties do not agree, the court shall appoint one or more referees, not exceeding three, who shall be free from all exception.

correspondences.note_fr: Les parties choisissent d’un commun accord le technicien, fixent sa mission, le rémunèrent selon leur accord et peuvent le révoquer unanimement. Le Missouri permet l’accord sur les referees et prévoit leur rémunération, mais dans le cadre d’une procédure de référence judiciaire et sans règle correspondante sur la révocation.
correspondences.note_en: The parties jointly choose the technician, define the mission, agree on compensation, and may unanimously revoke the appointment. Missouri permits agreement on referees and regulates compensation, but within a court-ordered reference framework and without a corresponding revocation rule.

correspondences.note_fr: Les techniciens peuvent être récusés pour les mêmes causes que les juges, avec une déclaration et une contestation selon un calendrier précis. Les règles et textes du Missouri imposent surtout que le master ou le referee soit désintéressé et exempt de motifs d’exception, sans prévoir l’ensemble des causes, délais et déclarations de l’article 234.
correspondences.note_en: Technicians may be challenged on the same grounds as judges, with specified timing and self-disclosure requirements. The Missouri provisions chiefly require masters or referees to be disinterested and free from exceptions, but do not reproduce the article’s full grounds, timing, or self-reporting procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: Le texte français permet au juge de désigner un tiers, de définir sa mission et le délai du rapport, et exige une compétence professionnelle dans le domaine. La Rule 68.01 prévoit la désignation d’un master ainsi que la définition de ses pouvoirs et du délai de son rapport; le RSMo 515.030 prévoit la nomination de referees aptes, sans exiger une compétence professionnelle déterminée.
correspondences.note_en: The French text permits the court to appoint a third party, define the assignment and reporting deadline, and requires professional competence in the relevant field. Rule 68.01 provides for appointing a master and defining the master’s powers and reporting deadline; RSMo 515.030 provides for appointing suitable referees without requiring a specified professional competence.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1450 réserve la mission d’arbitre à une personne physique jouissant de ses droits et limite le rôle d’une personne morale à l’organisation de l’arbitrage. Le § 515.030 RSMo prévoit la désignation de personnes aptes comme arbitres judiciaires, tandis que le § 515.040 impose leur impartialité, sans reprendre ces restrictions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1450 restricts the arbitral mandate to a natural person with full legal capacity and limits a legal entity to organizing the arbitration. RSMo 515.030 provides for appointing suitable referees, and RSMo 515.040 requires disinterestedness, but neither reproduces these restrictions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1451 impose un nombre impair d’arbitres et prévoit la complétion du tribunal lorsqu’un nombre pair a été désigné. Le § 515.030 RSMo permet la désignation d’un ou plusieurs référés, au plus trois, et le § 515.080 règle le fonctionnement collégial et la validité des actes de la majorité, sans exiger un nombre impair.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1451 requires an odd number of arbitrators and provides for completion of the tribunal when an even number was selected. RSMo 515.030 permits one or more referees, up to three, while RSMo 515.080 governs joint hearings and majority acts, without requiring an odd number.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1452 organise les modalités subsidiaires de désignation d’un arbitre unique ou de trois arbitres, avec intervention de l’organisateur ou du juge d’appui. Le § 515.030 RSMo prévoit seulement que les parties choisissent les référés ou que le tribunal les nomme en cas de désaccord, sans les mécanismes détaillés de désignation successive.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1452 establishes default appointment procedures for a sole arbitrator or a three-member tribunal, involving the administering person or supporting judge. RSMo 515.030 provides only that the parties select referees or that the court appoint them if they disagree, without the detailed sequential mechanisms.

correspondences.note_fr: En cas de désaccord entre plus de deux parties sur la constitution du tribunal arbitral, le juge d'appui ou l'organisateur désigne les arbitres. Le RSMo 515.030 permet au tribunal de nommer un ou plusieurs referees lorsque les parties ne s'accordent pas, dans une procédure de référence plutôt que d'arbitrage.
correspondences.note_en: If more than two parties cannot agree on constituting the arbitral tribunal, the support judge or arbitration organizer appoints the arbitrators. RSMo 515.030 permits the court to appoint one or more referees when the parties cannot agree, serving a comparable appointment function in a reference proceeding.

correspondences.note_fr: Tout différend relatif à la constitution du tribunal arbitral est réglé par l'organisateur ou le juge d'appui en l'absence d'accord. Le RSMo 515.030 vise seulement la nomination de referees lorsque les parties ne s'accordent pas, et non tout différend de constitution.
correspondences.note_en: Any dispute concerning constitution of the arbitral tribunal is resolved by the organizer or support judge if the parties do not agree. RSMo 515.030 covers only court appointment of referees when the parties cannot agree, not every constitution-related dispute.

norms.heading: Referees to be disinterested parties.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS

norms.text: No person shall be appointed referee who is of kin to either party, or is interested in the event of the action.

correspondences.note_fr: Le technicien doit révéler, avant d’accepter, toute circonstance affectant son indépendance ou son impartialité. Les règles du Missouri exigent surtout que le referee ou le master soit désintéressé, tandis que Rule 88.06 impose une divulgation des relations et intérêts susceptibles de créer un biais au médiateur.
correspondences.note_en: Before accepting, the technician must disclose circumstances affecting independence or impartiality. Missouri mainly requires referees and masters to be disinterested, while Rule 88.06 expressly requires mediators to disclose relationships and interests that could create bias or conflicts.

correspondences.note_fr: Les techniciens peuvent être récusés pour les mêmes causes que les juges, avec une déclaration et une contestation selon un calendrier précis. Les règles et textes du Missouri imposent surtout que le master ou le referee soit désintéressé et exempt de motifs d’exception, sans prévoir l’ensemble des causes, délais et déclarations de l’article 234.
correspondences.note_en: Technicians may be challenged on the same grounds as judges, with specified timing and self-disclosure requirements. The Missouri provisions chiefly require masters or referees to be disinterested and free from exceptions, but do not reproduce the article’s full grounds, timing, or self-reporting procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 237 impose au technicien d’exercer sa mission avec conscience, objectivité et impartialité. La Rule 68.03(c) et le RSMo 515.050 imposent un serment d’impartialité et de rapport juste, tandis que le RSMo 515.040 exclut les referees intéressés, sans formuler exactement une obligation générale de conduite.
correspondences.note_en: Article 237 requires the technician to perform the assignment conscientiously, objectively, and impartially. Rule 68.03(c) and RSMo 515.050 require an impartial oath and a just report, while RSMo 515.040 disqualifies interested referees, without stating the same general conduct duty.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1450 réserve la mission d’arbitre à une personne physique jouissant de ses droits et limite le rôle d’une personne morale à l’organisation de l’arbitrage. Le § 515.030 RSMo prévoit la désignation de personnes aptes comme arbitres judiciaires, tandis que le § 515.040 impose leur impartialité, sans reprendre ces restrictions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1450 restricts the arbitral mandate to a natural person with full legal capacity and limits a legal entity to organizing the arbitration. RSMo 515.030 provides for appointing suitable referees, and RSMo 515.040 requires disinterestedness, but neither reproduces these restrictions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose à l’arbitre de révéler les circonstances affectant son indépendance ou son impartialité et prévoit une procédure de contestation. Les articles du Missouri exigent seulement un arbitre désintéressé et un serment d’impartialité, sans obligation équivalente de révélation ni procédure de contestation.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires disclosure of circumstances affecting the arbitrator’s independence or impartiality and provides a challenge procedure. The Missouri provisions require only a disinterested referee and an oath of impartiality, without an equivalent disclosure duty or challenge process.

norms.text: Before proceeding to hear any testimony in the cause, they shall take and subscribe an oath before some officer duly authorized to administer an oath, faithfully and fairly to hear and examine the cause, and to make a just, impartial and true report, according to the best of their understanding, which oath shall be filed and returned with the award.

correspondences.note_fr: Le technicien doit agir avec diligence et impartialité, respecter la contradiction, exécuter personnellement sa mission et s’abstenir de toute appréciation juridique. Le Missouri impose diligence, impartialité et serment aux referees ou masters, mais les textes fournis ne reprennent pas l’ensemble de ces obligations.
correspondences.note_en: The technician must act diligently and impartially, respect adversarial procedure, perform the mission personally, and avoid legal judgments. Missouri imposes diligence, impartiality, and an oath on referees or masters, but the supplied provisions do not reproduce all of these duties.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 237 impose au technicien d’exercer sa mission avec conscience, objectivité et impartialité. La Rule 68.03(c) et le RSMo 515.050 imposent un serment d’impartialité et de rapport juste, tandis que le RSMo 515.040 exclut les referees intéressés, sans formuler exactement une obligation générale de conduite.
correspondences.note_en: Article 237 requires the technician to perform the assignment conscientiously, objectively, and impartially. Rule 68.03(c) and RSMo 515.050 require an impartial oath and a just report, while RSMo 515.040 disqualifies interested referees, without stating the same general conduct duty.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose à l’arbitre de révéler les circonstances affectant son indépendance ou son impartialité et prévoit une procédure de contestation. Les articles du Missouri exigent seulement un arbitre désintéressé et un serment d’impartialité, sans obligation équivalente de révélation ni procédure de contestation.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires disclosure of circumstances affecting the arbitrator’s independence or impartiality and provides a challenge procedure. The Missouri provisions require only a disinterested referee and an oath of impartiality, without an equivalent disclosure duty or challenge process.

norms.heading: Referees to hear and determine cause without delay.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: The referee or referees appointed in pursuance of any order of reference shall proceed with diligence to hear and determine the matter in controversy.

correspondences.note_fr: Le technicien doit agir avec diligence et impartialité, respecter la contradiction, exécuter personnellement sa mission et s’abstenir de toute appréciation juridique. Le Missouri impose diligence, impartialité et serment aux referees ou masters, mais les textes fournis ne reprennent pas l’ensemble de ces obligations.
correspondences.note_en: The technician must act diligently and impartially, respect adversarial procedure, perform the mission personally, and avoid legal judgments. Missouri imposes diligence, impartiality, and an oath on referees or masters, but the supplied provisions do not reproduce all of these duties.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise le signalement des difficultés d’un tiers chargé d’une mission et la prorogation judiciaire du délai de rapport. La Rule 68.01 encadre la mission, la diligence et le rapport du master; les sections 515.060 et 515.190 imposent également diligence et célérité, sans prévoir expressément cette procédure de prorogation.
correspondences.note_en: The article addresses difficulties encountered by an appointed third party and judicial extension of the reporting deadline. Rule 68.01 governs a master’s assignment, diligence, and report; sections 515.060 and 515.190 likewise require diligence and prompt reporting, but do not expressly provide this extension procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article oblige l’arbitre à poursuivre sa mission, sauf empêchement ou cause légitime, et organise le règlement du différend. Le Missouri impose au referee d’agir avec diligence et prévoit son remplacement en cas de décès ou de départ de l’État, mais ne reprend pas les mêmes motifs ni la même procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the arbitrator to continue until completion unless prevented or justified in resigning, and provides a dispute-resolution procedure. Missouri requires a referee to proceed diligently and provides replacement upon death or removal from the state, but does not reproduce the same grounds or procedure.

norms.heading: Appointment in case of death or removal of referee.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: In case of the death or removal from the state of a referee, another shall, if necessary and proper, be appointed to fill the vacancy.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet de saisir le juge pour les difficultés concernant la désignation, le maintien, la rémunération ou l’exécution de la mission du technicien. Les dispositions du Missouri permettent surtout de contraindre un referee à poursuivre sa mission, de régler sa rémunération et de pourvoir à son remplacement, mais sans reprendre la procédure française.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits referral to the judge for difficulties concerning an expert’s appointment, retention, compensation, or performance. Missouri provisions mainly address compelling a referee to proceed, fixing compensation, and replacing a referee, but do not reproduce the French procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 235 prévoit le remplacement du technicien en cas de récusation, refus, empêchement légitime ou manquement à ses devoirs. Les textes du Missouri prévoient le remplacement d’un referee ou d’un receiver en cas de décès, révocation, démission, manquement ou inaptitude, mais dans des institutions et sous des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 235 requires replacement of a technician after recusal, refusal, legitimate impediment, or breach of duties. The Missouri provisions provide replacement of a referee or receiver for death, removal, resignation, misconduct, or disqualification, but concern different institutions and conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article oblige l’arbitre à poursuivre sa mission, sauf empêchement ou cause légitime, et organise le règlement du différend. Le Missouri impose au referee d’agir avec diligence et prévoit son remplacement en cas de décès ou de départ de l’État, mais ne reprend pas les mêmes motifs ni la même procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the arbitrator to continue until completion unless prevented or justified in resigning, and provides a dispute-resolution procedure. Missouri requires a referee to proceed diligently and provides replacement upon death or removal from the state, but does not reproduce the same grounds or procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’instance arbitrale est suspendue après le décès, l’empêchement, l’abstention, la démission, la récusation ou la révocation d’un arbitre jusqu’à l’acceptation du remplaçant. Les textes du Missouri organisent le remplacement de certains auxiliaires ou décideurs, mais ne prévoient pas cette suspension arbitrale ni tous ces cas.
correspondences.note_en: The arbitral proceeding is suspended after an arbitrator’s death, incapacity, abstention, resignation, recusal, or removal until the replacement accepts the mandate. The Missouri provisions provide replacement mechanisms for certain commissioners, receivers, or referees, but not this arbitral stay or all of these grounds.

norms.heading: Referees must all meet and conduct hearing.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: If more than one referee be appointed, all the referees must meet together and hear all the proofs and allegations of the parties; but a report made and every other act done by a majority of them, shall be valid.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1451 impose un nombre impair d’arbitres et prévoit la complétion du tribunal lorsqu’un nombre pair a été désigné. RSMo 515.030 permits one or more referees, up to three, while RSMo 515.080 governs joint hearings and majority acts, without requiring an odd number.

norms.heading: Service of notices, how and by whom made.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: All notices required to be given by the referees or others, in the progress of a cause, shall be served by reading the same or delivering a copy to the person to be notified, and may be served by the sheriff or other officer authorized to serve process, whose return shall be evidence of the facts therein stated.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffe notifie la décision au tiers, recueille son acceptation et subordonne en principe le début de la mission au versement d’une provision. correspondences.note_en: The clerk notifies the appointee, obtains acceptance, and generally conditions commencement on payment of an advance. Rule 68.01 provides prompt delivery of the reference order and commencement of proceedings, but not acceptance or an advance; RSMo 515.100 concerns service of notices only.

norms.heading: Power to compel attendance of witnesses.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: They shall have the same power that may be given by law to associate circuit judges, to issue subpoenas for witnesses, and to compel their attendance by attachment, to administer oaths, and punish contempts committed in their presence during the hearing of the cause, and commit to the jail of the county such witnesses as refuse to testify.

correspondences.note_en: Article 242 allows a court-appointed technician to obtain information from any person, subject to identifying details, and permits a judicial hearing if useful. Rule 57.03 provides formal depositions of any person, while Rule 56.01 addresses identifying persons with discoverable knowledge; neither grants the same general power to a technician.

norms.heading: May compel parties to testify and produce documents.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: They shall have power, as courts of record have, to examine the parties on oath, to be administered by the referees, or either of them, and to require the production of all books, papers and documents in the custody or under the control of either party.

correspondences.note_fr: Les parties doivent communiquer les documents nécessaires au technicien, et le juge peut en ordonner la production sous astreinte. Le Missouri prévoit le pouvoir d’un referee d’exiger des documents, ainsi que des mesures de contrainte et sanctions pour défaut de production, mais ne reprend ni l’astreinte ni la faculté expresse pour le technicien de poursuivre sur les seuls éléments disponibles.
correspondences.note_en: The parties must provide documents needed by the technician, and the judge may compel production, including under a penalty. Missouri authorizes referees to require documents and provides compulsion and sanctions for nonproduction, but does not include the French penalty mechanism or the technician’s express ability to proceed on available materials.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 243 permet au technicien de demander tous documents aux parties et aux tiers, le juge intervenant en cas de difficulté. correspondences.note_fr: Le notaire convoque les parties, recueille les documents, signale les difficultés au juge et peut demander des mesures ou l’assistance d’un expert. correspondences.note_en: The notary convenes the parties, obtains documents, reports difficulties to the judge, and may seek measures or expert assistance. Rule 68.01 gives a master comparable procedural and evidence-gathering powers, and RSMo 515.130 addresses document production, but neither reproduces the full mechanism or expert-assistance provision.

norms.heading: Punishment for refusal to testify.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: If either party shall refuse to be sworn, or when sworn shall refuse to answer any proper question, the referees may imprison him until he consents to be sworn or to answer such question.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 57.03 prévoit le serment et l’avis de déposition, la Rule 43.01 la transmission des ordres au représentant ou à la partie, et le RSMo 515.150 une sanction en cas de refus de prêter serment ou de répondre. Ces textes ne prévoient ni l’avertissement pénal ni le régime français du serment décisoire.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 57.03 provides for the oath and deposition notice, Rule 43.01 for transmitting orders to counsel or a party, and RSMo 515.150 for refusal to be sworn or answer. These provisions do not provide the criminal warning or the French decisive-oath regime.

norms.heading: Testimony to be written — exceptions to be stated in report.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: All testimony taken before referees shall be reduced to writing, and if either party shall except to the competency of a witness or the admission or exclusion of evidence, or any other matter to which exceptions may be taken, the referees, if required, shall state the particulars of the exceptions in their report.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article prévoit que le technicien joigne au rapport les observations ou réclamations écrites des parties et indique les suites qui leur sont données. La Rule 68.01 prévoit la communication du rapport du master et les objections écrites; RSMo 515.170 et 515.200 organisent aussi la consignation et la présentation des exceptions, mais dans le cadre judiciaire des referees.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the technician to attach the parties’ written observations or objections to the report and state how they were addressed. Rule 68.01 provides service and written objections to a master’s report, while RSMo 515.170 and 515.200 address written exceptions in referee proceedings, but none has the same private-technician procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise la consignation de la consultation, oralement par procès-verbal ou par remise écrite au greffe, avec les pièces justificatives. Les dispositions du Missouri imposent la mise par écrit des témoignages et le retour au tribunal du rapport et des témoignages recueillis, mais ne règlent pas spécifiquement la consultation.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs recording the consultation, orally by minutes or in writing through filing with the clerk, with supporting documents. Missouri requires testimony to be reduced to writing and requires the report and testimony taken to be returned to the court, but does not specifically regulate consultations.

norms.heading: Court may compel referees to hear and report.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: The referees may be compelled, by the order of the court in which the cause is pending, to proceed to the hearing and make a report. And the court may require them to report their decision, in admitting or rejecting any witness, or the depositions of any witness or other testimony, in allowing or overruling any question to any witness, or answer thereto; and all proceedings by them, together with the testimony before them, and their reasons for allowing or disallowing any claim of either party.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet de saisir le juge pour les difficultés concernant la désignation, le maintien, la rémunération ou l’exécution de la mission du technicien. Les dispositions du Missouri permettent surtout de contraindre un referee à poursuivre sa mission, de régler sa rémunération et de pourvoir à son remplacement, mais sans reprendre la procédure française.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits referral to the judge for difficulties concerning an expert’s appointment, retention, compensation, or performance. Missouri provisions mainly address compelling a referee to proceed, fixing compensation, and replacing a referee, but do not reproduce the French procedure.

norms.heading: Report of referees.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: The referees shall, in all cases, report as speedily as possible, reciting the order of the court, and showing the notice to the parties, the time and place of stating the account or taking the testimony, and all other proceedings had, and return the same, together with the testimony taken, to the court.

correspondences.note_fr: Le constat est déposé au greffe, les constatations orales sont consignées et les pièces justificatives sont jointes au dossier. La Rule 68.01(g)(1) impose au master le dépôt d’un rapport avec la transcription, les preuves et les pièces ; le RSMo 515.190 impose également le retour du rapport et des témoignages au tribunal.
correspondences.note_en: The report is filed with the clerk, oral observations are recorded, and supporting documents are attached to the case file. Rule 68.01(g)(1) requires a master to file a report with the proceeding transcript, evidence, and exhibits; RSMo 515.190 likewise requires the report and testimony to be returned to the court.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise la consignation de la consultation, oralement par procès-verbal ou par remise écrite au greffe, avec les pièces justificatives. Les dispositions du Missouri imposent la mise par écrit des témoignages et le retour au tribunal du rapport et des témoignages recueillis, mais ne règlent pas spécifiquement la consultation.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs recording the consultation, orally by minutes or in writing through filing with the clerk, with supporting documents. Missouri requires testimony to be reduced to writing and requires the report and testimony taken to be returned to the court, but does not specifically regulate consultations.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise le signalement des difficultés d’un tiers chargé d’une mission et la prorogation judiciaire du délai de rapport. La Rule 68.01 encadre la mission, la diligence et le rapport du master; les sections 515.060 et 515.190 imposent également diligence et célérité, sans prévoir expressément cette procédure de prorogation.
correspondences.note_en: The article addresses difficulties encountered by an appointed third party and judicial extension of the reporting deadline. Rule 68.01 governs a master’s assignment, diligence, and report; sections 515.060 and 515.190 likewise require diligence and prompt reporting, but do not expressly provide this extension procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit une conciliation devant le juge puis un procès-verbal et un projet d’état liquidatif par le notaire. Les textes Missouri retenus concernent seulement la conduite et le rapport d’un master ou de referees; ils ne prévoient ni cette conciliation ni ce projet.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides for court-assisted conciliation followed by minutes and a draft liquidation statement prepared by the notary. The retained Missouri texts concern only proceedings and reporting by a master or referees; they provide neither the conciliation nor the liquidation draft.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: If exceptions are sustained the matter may again be referred, with instructions, if necessary, but if the report is confirmed by the court, judgment shall be rendered thereon in the same manner and with like effect as upon a special verdict.

Rules 96.16 and 515.210 address confirmation or recommittal of a report and entry of judgment; Rule 96.08 concerns determining the parties’ interests and ordering partition.

norms.heading: Compensation of referees.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: Referees, in the absence of any special agreement, shall receive such compensation for their services as the court in which the case is pending may allow, not exceeding ten dollars per day.

correspondences.note_fr: Les parties choisissent d’un commun accord le technicien, fixent sa mission, le rémunèrent selon leur accord et peuvent le révoquer unanimement. Le Missouri permet l’accord sur les referees et prévoit leur rémunération, mais dans le cadre d’une procédure de référence judiciaire et sans règle correspondante sur la révocation.
correspondences.note_en: The parties jointly choose the technician, define the mission, agree on compensation, and may unanimously revoke the appointment. Missouri permits agreement on referees and regulates compensation, but within a court-ordered reference framework and without a corresponding revocation rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet de saisir le juge pour les difficultés concernant la désignation, le maintien, la rémunération ou l’exécution de la mission du technicien. Les dispositions du Missouri permettent surtout de contraindre un referee à poursuivre sa mission, de régler sa rémunération et de pourvoir à son remplacement, mais sans reprendre la procédure française.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits referral to the judge for difficulties concerning an expert’s appointment, retention, compensation, or performance. Missouri provisions mainly address compelling a referee to proceed, fixing compensation, and replacing a referee, but do not reproduce the French procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 248 interdit au technicien de recevoir directement d’une partie toute rémunération ou remboursement de débours, sauf décision du juge. Les Rules 68.01 et 68.03 prévoient que la rémunération du master est fixée ou répartie par le tribunal, et le RSMo 515.220 soumet celle du referee à l’autorisation du tribunal, sans reprendre expressément l’interdiction de paiement direct.
correspondences.note_en: Article 248 bars a court-appointed technician from receiving remuneration or reimbursement directly from a party unless authorized by the judge. Rules 68.01 and 68.03 provide that a master’s compensation is directed by the court, and RSMo 515.220 makes a referee’s compensation court-allowed, but none expressly states the direct-payment prohibition.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 255 prévoit que le juge fixe la rémunération du constatant après justification de l’accomplissement de sa mission et peut lui délivrer un titre exécutoire. La Rule 68.01(a) règle la rémunération d’un master nommé par le tribunal, tandis que le RSMo 515.220 concerne celle des referees ; aucun des deux textes ne prévoit le titre exécutoire ni la condition d’achèvement de la mission.
correspondences.note_en: Article 255 provides that the judge fixes the court-appointed investigator’s compensation after proof that the assignment was completed and may issue an enforceable title. Rule 68.01(a) addresses compensation of a court-appointed master, and RSMo 515.220 addresses referees’ compensation; neither provides for an enforceable title or the completion-based condition.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 262 prévoit que le juge fixe la rémunération du consultant après justification de l’accomplissement de sa mission et peut lui délivrer un titre exécutoire. La Rule 68.01(a) et le RSMo 515.220 organisent la rémunération de personnes désignées comme master ou referee, mais ne prévoient pas la délivrance d’un titre exécutoire et imposent des cadres différents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 262 lets the judge set a consultant’s compensation after the mission is performed and permits issuance of an enforceable title. Rule 68.01(a) and RSMo 515.220 address compensation for court-appointed masters or referees, but do not provide for an enforceable title and operate under materially different institutional rules.

correspondences.note_fr: Le coût de la mission incombe à l’auteur du manquement; le juge fixe une provision proche de la rémunération prévisible et le délai de consignation, avec échéances éventuelles. La Rule 68.01 règle l’imputation de la rémunération, la Rule 77.02 la garantie des frais anticipés, et le RSMo 515.220 la rémunération des referees, sans reprendre ce mécanisme complet.
correspondences.note_en: The violator bears the mission cost, while the court fixes an advance approximating expected compensation and a deposit deadline, with possible installments. Rule 68.01 addresses allocation of a master’s compensation, Rule 77.02 security for anticipated costs, and RSMo 515.220 referee compensation, but none reproduces the full mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article règle l’acompte, la provision complémentaire et la conséquence du défaut de consignation pour un tiers chargé d’un rapport. La Rule 68.01 traite de la rémunération du master et de son imputation, la Rule 77.02 de la garantie des frais anticipés et la section 515.220 de la rémunération des arbitres, mais aucune ne reprend l’ensemble de ce mécanisme.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs an advance payment, supplemental security, and the consequence of failing to deposit it for a reporting third party. Rule 68.01 addresses a master’s compensation and its allocation, Rule 77.02 anticipated-cost security, and section 515.220 referee compensation, but none reproduces the complete mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Le tiers remet son rapport, transmet sa demande de rémunération aux parties et permet à l’auteur du manquement de présenter des observations dans les quinze jours. La Rule 68.01 prévoit le dépôt et la notification du rapport du master, tandis que les autres textes concernent la rémunération et les demandes de frais, sans reprendre exactement cette procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The third party files a report, serves the parties with a fee request, and allows the alleged violator fifteen days to comment. Rule 68.01 addresses filing and service of a master’s report, while the other provisions address compensation or fee applications without reproducing this exact procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge fixe la rémunération selon le travail accompli, règle les sommes consignées ou leur restitution, recueille les observations en cas de réduction et délivre un titre exécutoire. Les textes du Missouri permettent au tribunal de fixer ou d’allouer une rémunération et de taxer certains frais, mais ne prévoient pas l’ensemble de ces mécanismes.
correspondences.note_en: The court fixes compensation based on the work performed, applies or refunds deposited sums, invites comments before reducing the requested amount, and issues an enforceable title. The Missouri provisions allow court-set compensation or taxation of certain fees, but do not provide all of these mechanisms.

norms.heading: General and limited receivers.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text: A receiver shall be either a general receiver or a limited receiver. A receiver shall be a general receiver if the receiver is appointed to take possession and control of all or substantially all of a debtor's property and provided the power to liquidate such property. A receiver shall be a limited receiver if the receiver is appointed to take possession and control of only limited or specific property of a debtor, whether to preserve or to liquidate such property. A receiver appointed at the request of a person having a lien on or interest in specific property that constitutes all or substantially all of a debtor's property may be either a general receiver or a limited receiver. The court shall specify in the order appointing a receiver whether the receiver is appointed as a general receiver or as a limited receiver. The court by order, upon notice and a hearing, may convert either a general receiver into a limited receiver or a limited receiver into a general receiver for good cause shown. In the absence of a clear designation by the court of the type of receiver appointed, whether limited or general, the receiver shall be presumed to be a general receiver and shall have the rights, powers, and duties attendant thereto.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS

norms.text: Except as otherwise provided for by statute or court rule, before entering upon duties of receiver, a receiver shall execute a bond with one or more sureties approved by the court, in the amount the court specifies, conditioned that the receiver will faithfully discharge the duties of receiver in accordance with orders of the court and state law. correspondences.note_en: The article requires the sequestrator distributing the funds to provide security ensuring representation of the money. RSMo 515.530 requires a receiver’s bond, and Rule 96.31 requires a comparable bond from a land-sale commissioner, but under different procedures and institutions.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS

norms.heading: Estate property, turnover of upon demand — court action to compel.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text:
1. Upon demand by a receiver, any person, including the debtor, shall turn over any estate property that is within the possession or control of that person unless otherwise ordered by the court for good cause shown. A receiver by motion may seek to compel turnover of estate property as against any person over which the court first establishes jurisdiction, unless there exists a bona fide dispute with respect to the existence or nature of the receiver's possessory interest in the estate property, in which case turnover shall be sought by means of a legal action. In the absence of a bona fide dispute with respect to the receiver's right to possession of estate property, the failure to relinquish possession and control to the receiver shall be punishable as a contempt of the court.

2. Should the court after notice and a hearing pursuant to subsection 1 of this section order the turnover of property to the receiver, the party against which such order is made shall have the right to deliver a bond executed by such party as principal together with one or more sufficient sureties providing that the principal and each such surety shall each be bound to the receiver in double the amount of the value of the property to be turned over, should the property not be turned over to the receiver when such order becomes final. Absent such bond, the property ordered to be turned over to the receiver shall be immediately turned over to the receiver within ten days of the entry of such order.

norms.heading: Debtor to file schedules, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text:
1. Within thirty days after the date of appointment of a general receiver, the debtor shall file with the court and submit to the receiver the following schedules:

(1) A true list of all of the known creditors and applicable regulatory and taxing agencies of the debtor, including the mailing addresses for each, the amount and nature of their claims, and whether their claims are disputed; and

(2) A true list of all estate property, including the estimated liquidation value and location of the property and, if real property, a legal description thereof, as of the date of appointment of the receiver.

2. The Missouri supreme court may from time to time prescribe by court rule the schedules to be filed in receiverships as the supreme court shall deem appropriate to the effective administrations of sections 515.500 to 515.665.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article détaille les mentions obligatoires de l’inventaire, notamment les personnes, les lieux, les biens, leur valeur et l’actif et le passif. Le RSMo 515.560 exige des listes des créanciers et des biens avec leur valeur estimée et leur localisation, tandis que le RSMo 515.565 permet d’ordonner des inventaires, sans reprendre toutes les mentions françaises.
correspondences.note_en: The article specifies the required contents of an inventory, including persons, locations, assets, values, and the estate’s assets and liabilities. RSMo 515.560 requires schedules of creditors and estate property with estimated value and location, while RSMo 515.565 permits court-ordered inventories without reproducing all the French requirements.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet à l’inventaire notarié d’identifier les ayants droit et de décrire l’actif et le passif de la communauté. Le RSMo 515.560 couvre, en receivership, les listes de biens et de créanciers, mais pas l’identification des ayants droit ni l’inventaire notarié. Le RSMo 452.330 organise la répartition matrimoniale, non l’inventaire.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits a notarial inventory to identify persons entitled to the community or succession and to describe community assets and liabilities. RSMo 515.560 covers property and creditor schedules in receivership, but not identification of heirs or a notarial inventory. RSMo 452.330 governs marital distribution, not inventory.

norms.heading: Appraisal not required without court order.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 515 Referees and Receivers

norms.text:
1. A receiver shall not be obligated to obtain any appraisal or other independent valuation of property in the receiver's possession unless ordered by the court to do so.

2. A court may order the receiver to file such additional schedules, reports of assets, liabilities, claims, or inventories as necessary and proper.

3. Whenever a list or schedule required pursuant to this section is not prepared and filed as required by the debtor, the court may order the receiver, a petitioning creditor, or such other person as the court in its discretion deems appropriate to prepare and file such list or schedule within a time fixed by the court. The court may approve reimbursement of the cost incurred in complying with such order as an administrative expense.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet à certaines personnes de requérir un inventaire, notamment le curateur de la succession vacante. Le RSMo 515.565 permet au tribunal d’ordonner au receiver de préparer et déposer des inventaires, mais ne prévoit ni les mêmes requérants ni le même cadre successoral.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows specified persons, including a curator of a vacant estate, to require an inventory. RSMo 515.565 allows the court to order a receiver to prepare and file inventories, but does not provide the same applicants or probate framework.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article détaille les mentions obligatoires de l’inventaire, notamment les personnes, les lieux, les biens, leur valeur et l’actif et le passif. Le RSMo 515.560 exige des listes des créanciers et des biens avec leur valeur estimée et leur localisation, tandis que le RSMo 515.565 permet d’ordonner des inventaires, sans reprendre toutes les mentions françaises.
correspondences.note_en: The article specifies the required contents of an inventory, including persons, locations, assets, values, and the estate’s assets and liabilities. RSMo 515.560 requires schedules of creditors and estate property with estimated value and location, while RSMo 515.565 permits court-ordered inventories without reproducing all the French requirements.
